questions.text: A restaurant/cafeteria (V = 600 m3) with hard concrete walls and ceramic tile flooring currently has RT60 = 1.8 seconds (too reverberant). Target is 0.75 seconds for controlled noise. Calculate the additional absorption (in sabins) required.

options.text: A. 38 sabins
B. 75 sabins
C. 128 sabins
D. 205 sabins

questions.rationale: Sabine formula (SI): RT60 = 0.161 x V / A. Rearranging: A = 0.161 x V / RT60. Current absorption A_current = 0.161 x 600 / 1.8 = 53.7 sabins. Target absorption A_target = 0.161 x 600 / 0.75 = 128.8 sabins. Additional absorption required = A_target - A_current = 128.8 - 53.7 = 75.1 sabins (approximately 75 sabins). Correct answer is b. Option a (38 sabins) results from arithmetic error (e.g., dividing by 4 instead of subtracting). Option c (128 sabins) is the target total absorption A_target (not the additional amount; this is a common misreading). Option d (205 sabins) was the original erroneous marked answer and is off by a factor of 2.7 from the computed value; it would correspond to a target RT60 of 0.35 seconds (unrealistically low for a restaurant).

questions.text: A tropical climate causes polyurethane foam absorption panels (originally NRC 0.75) to degrade over 3 years of 80% RH exposure, reducing NRC to 0.55. A classroom retrofit originally specified 50 m2 of foam panels as the primary acoustic treatment. The classroom has volume V = 336 m3 and original RT60 = 0.70 s. The original total absorption (panels plus other room surfaces) was 77 sabins. What is the new RT60 after panel degradation, and is this acceptable for classroom acoustics?

options.text: A. RT60 increases to approximately 0.78 s (about 11% increase, borderline acceptable for classroom speech)
B. RT60 increases to approximately 0.85 s (about 21% increase, unacceptable for classroom speech intelligibility)
C. RT60 decreases to approximately 0.65 s (acceptable improvement)
D. RT60 remains stable at 0.70 s (no impact from material degradation)

questions.rationale: Panel absorption loss = (0.75 - 0.55) x 50 m2 = 0.20 x 50 = 10.0 sabins lost. New total absorption = 77 - 10 = 67 sabins. New RT60 = 0.161 x V / A_new = 0.161 x 336 / 67 = 0.81 s (approximately 0.80-0.85 s). Percent increase = (0.81 - 0.70) / 0.70 x 100 = 15.7% (in the 11-21% range). Correct answer is b. Option a understates the increase and the absorption loss. Option c is physically impossible: lowering NRC reduces absorption, which MUST increase RT60 (Sabine: RT60 inversely proportional to A). Option d is also physically impossible for the same reason. Cross-check of internal consistency: original RT60 = 0.161 x 336 / 77 = 0.70 s, matching the stem. After degradation: A = 77 - 10 = 67 sabins; RT60 = 0.161 x 336 / 67 = 0.81 s. ASHRAE/ANSI S12.60 recommends classroom RT60 <= 0.6-0.7s for speech intelligibility, so 0.81-0.85s is unacceptable.
